newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower in consolidation.

text.p: French stocks opened lower on Thursday as the market continued to digest its recent gains.

"It's a small consolidation and it's occurring calmly," a trader said. "None of the blue-chip CAC issues is losing much more than two percent. It's profit-taking affecting the whole of the market." Traders said the bourse's weakness did not put in doubt the market's broadly rising trend.

The leading CAC-40 index was down 14.09 points, or 0.54 percent, at 2,580.67 at 0945 GMT, after its 0.87 percent fall on Wednesday. The CAC-40 February futures contract was 16 points lower at 2,583. Volume was 950 million francs.
Credit Lyonnais certificates shot up 7.18 percent in early trading to 200 francs.
The newspaper Les Echos said the state-owned bank expects to report between 3.4 and 3.7 billion francs of net attributable profit for 1997 after a profit close to 300 million francs for 1996.

Accor shares were little changed, up 0.1 percent at 768 francs, after the sale by SGB of its eight percent stake in the French hotel group. Accor said the sale was carried out through placements to British and U.S. investors. The share is underpinned by the perception the capital is more dispersed.
